title: Attacking Graph Neural Networks with Bit Flips: Weisfeiler and Leman Go Indifferent

problem.claim: Bit flip attacks may compromise graph neural networks by altering their weights and biases.

gap.claim: Prior graph neural network attacks focused on graph poisoning and evasion, while bit flip attacks targeting network weights and biases were neglected.

contributions.claim: Directly applying a traditional bit flip attack to graph neural networks has limited effectiveness.
The Injectivity Bit Flip Attack targets learnable neighborhood aggregation functions in quantized message passing neural networks.
The attack uses mathematical properties of certain graph neural networks to impair graph-structure distinction and Weisfeiler-Leman expressivity.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The attack degraded maximal expressive Graph Isomorphism Networks trained on graph property prediction datasets to random output by flipping only a small fraction of the network's bits.
The attack had higher destructive power than traditional bit flip attacks transferred from convolutional neural networks.
The approach was confirmed by extensive empirical results.

narrative_sequence.summary: Existing graph neural network attacks focused on poisoning and evasion, unlike the recognized bit flip threat in convolutional neural networks.
A traditional bit flip attack has limited effectiveness when directly applied to graph neural networks.
The authors introduce the Injectivity Bit Flip Attack for graph neural networks.

The attack targets learnable neighborhood aggregation functions to reduce graph-structure discrimination and Weisfeiler-Leman expressivity, while exploiting mathematical properties of certain architectures.

On graph property prediction datasets, the attack reportedly reduced maximal expressive Graph Isomorphism Networks to random output with a small fraction of bit flips and exceeded transferred traditional attacks in destructive power.

source_observation.claim: Attacks that exploit architecture-specific mathematical properties can substantially increase the vulnerability of graph neural networks to bit flips.

interpretation.claim: Threat models should account for structural properties of the target architecture rather than assume attacks transfer uniformly across model families.

application.claim: Evaluate fault-injection robustness using attacks designed around the target model's aggregation and expressivity mechanisms.

exception.claim: The abstract limits the claim to certain graph neural networks and does not establish general vulnerability across all architectures or tasks.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the exact bit-flip budget.
The abstract does not identify the evaluated datasets or graph neural network configurations.
The abstract does not provide independent verification of the reported results.
